definition: Weaviate is an open-source vector database with built-in vectorisers, hybrid (keyword + vector) search and generative modules.
details: Created by Bob van Luijt and team in 2019; developed by Weaviate B.V. (Amsterdam).

explainer.lead: How to install Weaviate, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import weaviate

client = weaviate.connect_to_local()        # docker run -p 8080:8080 semitechnologies/weaviate
docs = client.collections.create("Doc")
docs.data.insert({"text": "Cats purr when happy."}, vector=[0.1, 0.9, 0.0])
print(docs.query.near_vector([0.1, 0.8, 0.1], limit=1).objects[0].properties)
client.close()

explainer.inAi: Hybrid search often beats pure vector search for RAG; Weaviate does both in one query.

tiers.eli5: Think of a library where books are shelved by meaning rather than title, and the librarian can also look things up by exact words and even write you a summary from what they find.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as the retrieval store behind semantic search and RAG pipelines, relying on built-in vectorisers so text is embedded on ingestion and hybrid search blends keyword and vector scores. A common pitfall is assuming the default vectoriser matches your domain; mismatched embeddings silently degrade recall.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a database that indexes high-dimensional vectors and supports approximate nearest-neighbour queries, with hybrid search combining vector similarity and keyword scoring. Recall depends on the index's approximation parameters, so exact nearest neighbours are not guaranteed.

explainer.example: A support team indexes 200,000 help articles; a query like 'reset my password' returns semantically close articles via vector search and exact-term matches via keyword search, merged into one ranked list.
